summary:
Our project, Silicon, aims to find an analog in Kazakhstan. We have scanned through tons of NASA data in order to find our coordinates for an analog, which addresses the challenge by finding a suitable analog in a region that is isn't explored as much.
We used NASA data in three main ways in the report:
Surface temperature (MODIS): MOD11A1 v061 daily land surface temperature at 1 km, tile h21v04, for 1 June to 31 August 2023. We used the day-minus-night difference to find a uniform, high-swing desert site on the Ustyurt Plateau margin (mean swing 25.3 °C, spread 1.4 °C).
Terrain (SRTM and MOLA): SRTM 1 arc-second tiles gave the Earth site’s slope and roughness. MOLA topography tiles from the PDS Geosciences Node gave roughness for Gale (Bradbury Landing) and Jezero. All three were compared at the same ~450 m scale.
Thermal inertia (THEMIS): the Jezero THEMIS map (Zenodo record 4931348) and the 2026 Gale THEMIS map (Zenodo record 23527756, MC-23, 1 km/pixel). The Gale map was used after the USGS and ASU download links failed.
NASA sources also supplied the Apollo 11 landing coordinates, the Planetary Fact Sheet values for Mars gravity and atmosphere, the NASA Worldview imagery check, and the lunar power-system report used as a cross-check on the Diviner values.
details:
The Ustyurt Plateau in Kazakhstan is the focus of this project. The Ustyurt Plateau is considered an Earth‑based research site where conditions similar to those on the Moon and Mars can be studied. The Ustyurt Plateau was chosen to see whether a landscape in Kazakhstan could show similarities to the surfaces astronauts and robotic missions may encounter on other planets.

To investigate this NASAs MODIS Terra satellite data was used to study surface temperatures from June to August 2023. The Ustyurt Plateau was observed for 92 days. The Ustyurt Plateau showed an average daytime‑to‑nighttime temperature difference of 25.3°C. The Ustyurt Plateaus geological composition, surface roughness and terrain were studied and the Ustyurt Plateau was compared with data from the Moon and Mars.

Benefits: The Ustyurt Plateau offers a natural environment that could be useful for preliminary testing of robotic rovers, navigation systems, thermal equipment and geological research. Studying these conditions on Earth can help researchers understand how equipment might perform before being used in space missions.

Intended impact: The Ustyurt Plateau is hoped to bring attention to Kazakhstans contribution to planetary science and demonstrate that Kazakhstan has landscapes worth considering for international space research. The Ustyurt Plateau also shows how satellite technology can help identify and study locations that may support lunar and Mars exploration.

Tools and technologies: Python was used for data processing and calculations. PyHDF was used to read satellite data. GDAL was used for processing. NASA datasets including MODIS Terra, SRTM, MOLA and THEMIS were used. NASA Worldview was also used to examine the Ustyurt Plateau.

Creativity and innovation: What makes the Ustyurt Plateau project different is its focus on Kazakhstan. The Ustyurt Plateau is not commonly discussed as an analog site yet its dry landscape, layered rock formations, gypsum‑bearing limestone and relatively uniform surface conditions make the Ustyurt Plateau an interesting candidate for further research. The Ustyurt Plateau was chosen to explore the potential of a location in Kazakhstan rather than limit the search to more familiar desert environments.

Factors considered: The Ustyurt Plateau was examined for temperature differences, geological composition, terrain roughness, surface uniformity, data accuracy and environmental protection. The Ustyurt Plateau was also examined for differences between Earth and the Moon and Mars, gravity, atmospheric pressure and radiation. These differences are important because the Ustyurt Plateau cannot recreate the conditions of another planet but the Ustyurt Plateau may still be useful for specific types of research and testing.

Overall the Ustyurt Plateau project is, about connecting Kazakhstans landscape with the future of space exploration. The Ustyurt Plateau shows how local environments, combined with NASAs satellite data can contribute to scientific research.
